title: bk export — emit a vectorizable bead corpus
description:
# bk export — emit a vectorizable bead corpus

## Summary

Add a `bk export` subcommand that emits a normalized, curated, indexable
representation of beads across one or more projects, designed to be fed into
ANY vector store (downstream-svc vector, pgvector, etc.). Beekeeper does NOT embed,
index, or own a vector — it only produces a clean corpus. The vector layer
lives outside the binary (a separate `bkx`/downstream-svc-app consumer).

## Why bk is the right tap (vs reading raw beads/issues from GitHub)

A naive indexer pointed straight at `issues.jsonl` on a repo's default branch
gets a raw, possibly-stale, per-repo, un-normalized, noisy view. `bk` already
does the work that makes the corpus correct and high-signal:

1. Authoritative / de-drifted state — bead state lives on a sync branch; trunk
   holds stale copies and feature branches strand writes. `bk` (trunk-sync /
   drift logic) knows where the reconciled truth is, so the export reflects the
   CURRENT state, not "whatever is on main".
2. Cross-project aggregation + identity normalization — walks all `.beads/`
   hives and canonicalizes drifted actor handles.
3. Resolved cross-bead relationships — dependency graph (blocks/blocked-by),
   lease/assignee state, supersession links — computed across beads, absent
   from any single raw issue.
4. Stable schema across `bd` versions — one consistent output shape so the
   indexer writes no per-source glue.
5. Curation — classify routine vs decision/data-bearing beads so the index is
   high-signal (the biggest quality lever for a knowledge/decision index).

## Command

    bk export [paths...] [flags]

Walks the given paths (default: cwd) for `.beads/` projects, same discovery as
`bk doctor` / `bk board`. Read-only; never mutates beads, never shells out to
mutate `bd`.

## Output

- One document per bead. Default format NDJSON (one JSON object per line) for
  streaming into ingest pipelines; `--format json` for a single array.
- Stable, documented schema (below). Deterministic field ordering.

### Document schema (per bead)

- `id` — bead id (e.g. `bkg-9cs`). Stable; use as the vector `source_uri` for
  idempotent overwrite-on-change.
- `repo` — originating project (path or repo slug).
- `title`
- `body` — issue description.
- `comments` — flattened comment thread (the richest rationale signal),
  optionally concatenated into `text` (see flags).
- `text` — assembled embedding payload (title + body + comments per flags).
- `status`, `issue_type`, `priority`, `labels`, `assignee`.
- `deps` — resolved `{blocks: [...], blocked_by: [...]}`.
- `created_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`.
- Computed curation metadata:
  - `is_routine` (bool) — heuristic: short body, no rationale language, chore/
    typo/bump-style.
  - `is_decision` (bool) — label-driven first (`decision`/`adr`/`architecture`),
    text-signal fallback ("because", "decided", "rejected", "instead of").
  - `richness` (number) — body+comment length / signal score.
  - `superseded_by` — bead id(s) that reverse/replace this one, when derivable
    from links.

Classification is emitted as METADATA FLAGS, never as deletion — the indexer or
the query decides what to filter. Keeps the export a faithful projection
(consistent with the "owns no issue data" tenet) and lets the caller change
their mind at query time.

## Tuning parameters (the fine-tuning the export should expose)

- `--format ndjson|json` (default ndjson).
- `--output PATH` / stdout default.
- `--status open|closed|all` (default all).
- `--type feature,task,...` / `--labels a,b` — include/exclude filters.
- `--since DATE` — only beads updated after DATE (incremental re-index).
- `--include-comments` (default true) / `--no-comments`.
- `--include-closed` (default true) — closed beads are valuable as prior art for
  decision retrieval.
- `--classify` (default true) — compute `is_routine`/`is_decision`/`richness`.
- `--min-richness N` — drop low-signal beads below a threshold (off by default;
  prefer flags over deletion).
- `--decisions-only` — convenience filter to `is_decision=true`.
- `--text-template` — control how `text` is assembled (e.g.
  `"{{title}}\n\n{{body}}\n\n{{comments}}"`).
- `--fields a,b,c` — project a subset of schema fields.
- `--repo-filter GLOB` — restrict to matching projects (cross-project tap).
- `--redact` — optional scrub of emails/tokens from text.

Classification heuristics MUST be configurable (label-driven first, text/length
fallback) and documented as a ranking aid, not ground truth.

## Non-goals (scope guard)

- No embedding, no vector index, no server inside `bk`. Keeps the
  single-static-binary, zero-dependency, no-server properties intact.
- No new source of truth — export is a derived, rebuildable projection of the
  JSONL, exactly like the SQLite cache.
- The vector consumer (`bkx` / downstream-svc app + sync job) is a SEPARATE work item.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bk export` discovers `.beads/` across given paths and emits one document per
  bead in NDJSON (default) and JSON.
- Output reflects authoritative/reconciled bead state (not stale trunk copies)
  and normalized actor identities.
- Schema includes title/body/comments/status/type/labels/assignee/deps/
  timestamps + `is_routine`/`is_decision`/`richness`/`superseded_by`.
- All tuning flags above implemented with sensible defaults; `--since` enables
  incremental re-index; `--decisions-only` and `--min-richness` filter signal.
- Deterministic output (stable ordering) so re-runs diff cleanly.
- Read-only: never mutates beads/JSONL, never touches the daemon.
- Unit tests for schema, filters, classification heuristics, and
  authoritative-state selection.
- README documents the command, schema, and flags.

## Cross-platform release (must ship like the rest of bk)

- Built and released for macOS, Linux, and Windows via the existing goreleaser
  pipeline.
- Homebrew tap (`brew install theaichimera/tap/bk`) updated on release.
- Windows `.zip` asset in the GitHub release.
- Version bump + changelog entry; docs-only `docs:` excluded from changelog as
  configured.

## Open questions

- Should `text` assembly default to including comments, or make it opt-in for
  cost? (Leaning: include by default — comments carry the rationale.)
- Supersession links: derivable from existing dep types, or need a new link
  kind in `bd`?
- Where does `bk export` draw the authoritative-state line for a dirty working
  tree / unsynced sync branch — warn, or refuse, or export-as-of-sync-branch?
close_reason: completed in 384e3da

title: bk: drift guard is push-gated — add commit-time/local drift detection to close the silent-accumulation window
description: Evidence from downstream-app (real incident, 2026-06-01): a branch 513 commits behind origin/main accumulated 154 pr-beads regressions (134 dropped-record, 10 status-rewind, 10 stale-timestamp) over 6 days with ZERO signal until a human manually ran bk doctor. Root-cause chain: (1) the bd daemon auto-commits 'bd sync' snapshots at COMMIT time on the stale branch; (2) bk's drift guard (trunk-sync) is PUSH-gated, but the branch had no upstream so nothing was ever pushed -> pre-push guard never fires; (3) the only installed hook that DID fire is bd's pre-commit, which runs 'bd sync --flush-only' and performs no drift check (see .git/hooks/pre-commit lines 1-7,39-44 — pure flush, happily commits a stale snapshot). Net: an unguarded window between manual 'bk doctor' and pre-push where drift originates and compounds locally. FIX DIRECTION: bk install-hooks should offer a pre-commit drift guard (or augment bd's flush hook) that cheaply warns/refuses when the current branch is >N commits behind base, sync.branch is unset, or bd state is needs_manual_sync — converting a silent 6-day drift into a first-commit warning. Consider a 'bk doctor --gate' fast exit-code mode agents can run on repo entry. Partly bd territory: daemon should not silently auto-commit bd-sync on a wildly-behind, upstream-less branch.
close_reason: shipped in 79f5814 — internal/drift + pre-commit drift gate + bk doctor --gate

title: bk doctor: flag when bk guard hooks are not installed (only bd flush hook present)
description: Evidence from downstream-app (2026-06-01): the repo had .git/hooks/pre-commit + post-merge, but those are bd's OWN hooks (pre-commit = 'bd sync --flush-only', no drift check), and there was NO pre-push hook — i.e. 'bk install-hooks' was never run. So the only bead protection was manual bk doctor. There is currently no signal that bk's guard hooks are absent; an operator/agent has no way to know they're unprotected. FIX DIRECTION: add a bk doctor check that detects when a bead repo is missing bk's guard hook(s) (distinguishing bk hooks from bd's flush-only pre-commit) and emits a YELLOW with remediation 'bk install-hooks'. Make 'bk install-hooks' idempotent/re-runnable so the remediation is safe to suggest. Pairs with bkg-59b (commit-time drift guard) — bkg-59b adds the guard; this bead makes its absence self-surfacing. Optional: recommend bk install-hooks as part of repo onboarding docs.
close_reason: shipped in 67d0651 — doctor.checkBkHooks + harness goOnlyCheckNames

title: bk lease release hard-fails when .beadkeeper/identity.toml is missing
description: Observed in downstream-svc-v2 repo. 'bk lease release <id>' errors: 'identity not configured at ./.beadkeeper/identity.toml. Leasing requires a canonical-handle map.' This blocks releasing a stale lease that bk doctor itself flagged. Expected: bk should resolve identity from bk identity / git config, or degrade to a best-effort release with a clear one-line setup hint, rather than hard-blocking. Repro: in a repo without .beadkeeper/identity.toml, run bk doctor (flags stale lease), then bk lease release <id> -> error.
design: AUDIT (read-only, beekeeper-go @754f723): REAL_GAP. lease.ResolveCaller (internal/lease/lease.go:138-144) hard-fails when .beadkeeper/identity.toml is missing, but identity is documented OPT-IN (cmd/bk/identity.go:16-18). cmd/bk/lease.go:62-67 calls ResolveCaller before Release so the AlreadyReleased no-op path (lease.go:244-251) is unreachable; --as handle does not bypass. Actual release mutation (lease.go:265) is 'bd update <id> --status open --assignee empty' which works with a raw handle. FIX (~10 lines): in ResolveCaller, when cfg==nil fall through to RawHandle() (git user.email/BD_ACTOR) instead of erroring; keep 'unknown alias' error only when cfg present. Files: internal/lease/lease.go + lease_test.go (no-config-degrades test).
close_reason: fixed in 6c24bf6 — ResolveCaller degrades to raw handle when identity.toml missing

Separate repo theaichimera/beekeeper-go, binary 'bk'. Stays a wrapper around git/bd/ps (no reimplementation, no SQLite driver). Behavioral parity with the Python tool is the bar: output, exit codes, refusal conditions. Full spec: docs/handoff/EPIC.md.

title: Backlog-hygiene tooling: deterministic bk commands so agents stop hand-rolling bd/jq/git
description:
## Why

During a real review of the `downstream-app` backlog (627 beads: 328 closed, 33 in_progress, 266 open), `bk` could answer almost none of the questions an operator/agent actually asks about backlog health. The agent had to hand-roll everything with raw tools:

- status counts / % complete  → `bd list --json | jq 'group_by(.status)'`
- stale-WIP ranking           → `bd list --json | jq` over `updated_at`
- "shipped but never closed"  → `git log origin/main --grep=downstream-app-<id>` per bead

That investigation found ~18 of 33 `in_progress` beads were already shipped (each had a merged PR whose title named the bead) but never closed — i.e. real WIP was ~12, not 33. `bk` surfaced none of this.

## Goal

The whole point of `bk` is that an agent should NOT have to go renegade with bespoke `bd`/`jq`/`git` pipelines every time. These should be **deterministic, repeatable, scriptable** commands with `--json` and stable exit codes — the same contract as the existing `guard` family.

`bk` today is strong on infrastructure health (sync, daemons, leases, merge-stomp prevention via `pr-beads`) but has almost nothing for **backlog hygiene**. This epic closes that gap.

## Children

1. `bk board --summary` / `--json` — aggregate counts, % complete, machine-readable board.
2. Stale-WIP detection — flag `in_progress` beads untouched > N days (in `doctor` + board summary).
3. `bk guard stale-beads` — git↔backlog reconciliation: beads that look shipped (id in a merged PR/commit title on the default branch) but are still open/in_progress.

## Principle

Anything an agent currently does to a `.beads/` backlog with raw `jq`/`git` and gets a useful answer is a candidate `bk` command. Determinism + `--json` + exit codes so it can run in CI and in agent loops.
close_reason: epic complete: board summary/json + stale-wip + guard stale-beads all merged

title: bk board --summary / --json (aggregate counts, % complete, machine-readable)
description:
## Problem

`bk board` dumps every ready bead (250+ wrapped lines on downstream-app) with no aggregate view and no machine-readable output. To answer "how are we doing?" the agent fell back to `bd list --json | jq`.

## Deliverable

Add an aggregate/summary mode and JSON output to `bk board`.

- `bk board --summary <path>`: human-readable rollup, no per-bead dump:
  - total beads; counts by status (open / in_progress / blocked / closed)
  - % complete (closed / total)
  - active (non-closed) counts by priority (P0..P4)
  - in_progress count + stale-in_progress count (ties into child .2)
- `bk board --json <path>`: machine-readable — the same aggregates PLUS the ready/in_progress/blocked lists, so agents can script against it instead of parsing `bd` output.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bk board --summary` on downstream-app prints the rollup (e.g. TOTAL 627 / closed 328 / in_progress 33 / open 266 / 52% complete / P0:3 P1:53 ...) in <1s, no per-bead spam.
- `bk board --json` emits valid JSON with `totals`, `by_status`, `by_priority`, and the lists; deterministic ordering.
- Existing default `bk board` behavior unchanged (back-compat).
- Works across multiple projects when given a parent dir (same discovery as today).
- Exit codes per bk contract; `--json` never interleaves human text.

## Motivating example

downstream-app review needed status counts + % complete; `bk board` couldn't provide them — derived via `bd list --json | jq group_by(.status)`.
acceptance_criteria: bk board --summary prints status/priority rollup + % complete with no per-bead dump; bk board --json emits deterministic JSON aggregates+lists; default board unchanged.
close_reason: shipped in #17/#18/#19

title: Stale-WIP detection: flag in_progress beads untouched > N days (doctor + board)
description:
## Problem

Nothing in `bk` flags beads parked in `in_progress` for a long time. downstream-app had 33 in_progress, 22 of them untouched for 7+ days (one since 2026-05-06, ~26 days). This WIP bloat is invisible until someone manually ranks `bd list --json` by `updated_at`.

## Deliverable

Stale-WIP detection as a first-class `bk` signal.

- A `bk doctor` check that flags `in_progress` (and optionally `open`/`blocked`) beads whose `updated_at` is older than a threshold.
  - Default threshold: 7 days. Configurable via flag (`--stale-days N`) and/or `.beads/config.json`.
  - Severity: YELLOW (advisory) by default; count surfaced in the project health line, e.g. "pr-wip: 22 in_progress beads stale >7d (oldest 26d: downstream-app-6ml)".
- Surface the same count in `bk board --summary` (child .1).

## Acceptance criteria

- `bk doctor` on a repo with stale in_progress beads emits a YELLOW `stale-wip` check naming the count, the threshold, and the oldest offender.
- Threshold configurable; `--stale-days 0` disables the check.
- Timestamp parsing handles real bead `updated_at` values: RFC3339 WITH timezone offsets and fractional seconds (e.g. `2026-05-06T16:50:40.133129+03:00`) — note jq's `fromdateiso8601` chokes on these, so the Go impl must parse offsets properly.
- `--json` output lists offending bead ids + ages.
- Clean repos (no stale WIP) emit no check (silent), consistent with other doctor checks.

## Motivating example

downstream-app: 33 in_progress, 22 stale >7d — computed by hand from `updated_at`. `bk` should report this automatically.
acceptance_criteria: bk doctor emits YELLOW stale-wip check (count + threshold + oldest offender); threshold configurable; parses RFC3339 with TZ offset + fractional seconds; --json lists offenders; silent when clean.
close_reason: shipped in #17/#18/#19

title: bk guard stale-beads: git<->backlog reconciliation (shipped-but-not-closed)
description:
## Problem (highest-value gap)

A bead's work often lands (PR merged to the default branch, commit/PR title naming the bead id) but the bead is never moved to `closed`. On downstream-app this hid ~18 of 33 `in_progress` beads — real WIP was ~12. Detecting this today means running `git log origin/<default> --grep=<prefix>-<id>` per bead by hand. This is the post-merge analogue of `bk guard pr-beads` (bkg-lrc): pr-beads catches backlog drift GOING INTO a merge; this catches drift that ACCUMULATES after merges.

## Deliverable

`bk guard stale-beads` (a.k.a. backlog reconciliation) — deterministic git↔backlog drift report.

- Derive the bead-id prefix from `.beads/` (e.g. `downstream-app-`).
- Scan merged commits on the default branch (`git log <branch> --grep`) for bead-id references in commit/PR titles. (Optionally cross-check merged PR titles via the GitHub API when a token is present; git-log-only must work offline.)
- Report two classes:
  - **shipped-not-closed (RED/YELLOW):** bead in `open`/`in_progress` whose id appears in a merged commit/PR title on the default branch. Include the bead id, status, and the landing commit/PR (sha + subject).
  - **closed-no-landing (advisory):** `closed` bead with no referencing commit — possible mis-close. (Lower severity; behind a flag is fine.)
- Match precision: prefer the id appearing as a delimited token in the SUBJECT (e.g. `downstream-app-xymh)` / `(downstream-app-xymh)`), not just anywhere in the body, to avoid tangential-reference false positives (the downstream-app run saw `4i54` referenced in 8 commits but only some were the actual fix; `afby`/`6ml` were referenced tangentially and were NOT done — the tool must not over-claim).

## Acceptance criteria

- `bk guard stale-beads <path>` lists shipped-not-closed beads with their landing PR/commit. On downstream-app it must flag at least: `xymh`#736, `o1b4`#737, `0dh4`/`fz56`#738, `e42f`#777, `1k8x.1`#831, `1k8x.2`#834, `1k8x.5`#836, `1k8x.6`#837, `1k8x.7`#833, `1k8x.9`#839, `4yzw`#841, `p561`#842, `lgd2`#843, `4dll`#844, `h2ml.1`#876.
- Must NOT flag tangential-only references as shipped (e.g. `afby`, `6ml`).
- `--json` output (bead id, status, landing sha/subject/PR#); deterministic ordering.
- Configurable lookback / branch / prefix; exit codes per bk contract (RED => non-zero so it can gate CI).
- Offline mode (git-log only) works without any GitHub token.
- Optional `--fix` is OUT OF SCOPE for v1 (report only) — closing is a human/agent decision; but the JSON should be shaped so an agent can drive `bd close <id> --reason "shipped in #<PR>"` deterministically.

## Motivating example

This exact downstream-app run: ~18 in_progress beads already shipped, found via manual `git log --grep`. `bk guard stale-beads` would have produced the same list deterministically in one command.
acceptance_criteria: Flags open/in_progress beads whose id is in a merged commit/PR subject on default branch, with landing PR/commit; must catch the downstream-app set (xymh#736..h2ml.1#876) and must NOT flag tangential refs (afby/6ml); --json deterministic; offline git-only works; RED=>nonzero for CI.
close_reason: shipped in #17/#18/#19

title: bk guard pr-beads — content-aware backlog-regression gate for PRs
description:
## Problem

A feature branch cut from main carries a snapshot of `.beads/issues.jsonl`. While the branch lives, the daemon advances bead state on main. Merging the branch reverts the backlog file — status rewind, assignee loss, dropped records.

Real incident: a branch was cut when bead `.24` was `open`; main advanced it to `in_progress` (assignee `queryparser-agent`); the branch still carried the old file. Merging would silently revert `.24` to `open` and drop the assignee. GitHub flagged mergeability UNKNOWN.

`bk guard sync-branch` does NOT catch this: `_branch_records_subset_of_sync` compares by record **id**, not content, and explicitly assumes "bead edits only ever originate on the sync branch"; it also scans only local `refs/heads`, never an incoming PR.

## Deliverable

`bk guard pr-beads` — diffs bead JSONL between a base and head ref and reports backlog regressions; runnable as a GitHub PR/CI gate.

## Detection (per bead id present in BOTH base and head)

- status rewind: rank open=0, in_progress=1, blocked=1, closed=2; head.rank < base.rank => RED
- assignee loss/overwrite: base assignee set, head clears/changes => RED
- stale timestamp: if updated_at/modified present, head older than base for same id => RED (prefer this signal)
- dropped record: id in base, absent in head => RED
- forward-only (new ids; head strictly newer) => GREEN

## Policies (--policy)

- regression (default): only regressions fail (beads-on-main repos)
- no-beads (strict): ANY `.beads/issues.jsonl` modification in base..head fails (dedicated-sync-branch repos)

## CLI / CI contract

`bk guard pr-beads --base <ref> --head <ref> [--policy regression|no-beads] [--json] [--strict]`
Defaults: base = $GITHUB_BASE_REF or origin/<default>; head = HEAD.
Exit codes (mirror bk): 0 clean | 2 RED regression | 1 generic/--strict-yellow | 64 usage | 127 git missing.
`--json`: findings list {id, field, kind, base_value, head_value}.

## Integration

- bk doctor: opt-in check (skipped unless base ref resolvable)
- bk install-hooks: extend pre-push to optionally run --policy no-beads vs upstream sync branch; reuse hook marker; honor BEADKEEPER_SKIP_HOOK / BEADKEEPER_BLOCK_ON_RED
- docs: README guard section + copy-paste GitHub Actions snippet

## Subtasks

1. internal/prbeads (or internal/guard) detection core + table-driven tests
2. cmd/bk wiring: `guard pr-beads` flags, exit codes, --json
3. base/head ref resolution (merge-base, GITHUB_BASE_REF) in internal/git
4. doctor integration (opt-in) + install-hooks pre-push extension
5. docs: README guard section + GitHub Actions workflow snippet
6. diff-harness parity entry (or documented Go-only divergence in docs/PARITY.md)

## Done when

- The PR #13 scenario (same id, open <- in_progress, assignee dropped) is flagged RED
- A forward-only change (new bead, or open -> in_progress on head) is GREEN
- no-beads policy fails on any `.beads/issues.jsonl` diff
- Runs headless in CI with correct exit codes; GOOS=windows build OK; golangci-lint + go test green on all OSes
acceptance_criteria: PR #13 scenario flagged RED; forward-only changes GREEN; no-beads policy fails on any .beads/issues.jsonl diff; headless CI exit codes correct; GOOS=windows build + lint + tests green on all OSes.
close_reason: Closed

title: bk doctor stale-lease detection has no working release path (assignee vs lease mismatch)
description: bk doctor reports stale lease(s) keyed on the assignee field, but bk lease release uses a different lease abstraction gated behind identity.toml, and bd has no unassign verb (bd update --assignee empty is a no-op). Net: doctor flags a lease the operator cannot clear except by closing the bead. Make doctor lease concept and bk lease release agree, or provide a release that clears the assignee doctor keys on. Related: bkg-8nw.

title: stale-beads v2 hardening: precision + authoritative status + apply mode
description:
## Why

`bk guard stale-beads` (bkg-bqa.3) was dogfooded against the real `downstream-app` backlog (48 findings) and then used to close 40 shipped-but-not-closed beads. The exercise surfaced three concrete defects the tool should fix so the WHOLE workflow — detect AND reconcile — is deterministic and an agent never has to hand-run `bd` in a shell loop.

Observed on 2026-06-01:
- 7 of 48 findings (15%) were FALSE POSITIVES: the "landing" commit was the bead's own filing/spec commit, not implementation.
- After `bd close downstream-app-l6q` (bd DB = closed), the guard STILL reported l6q as shipped-not-closed, because it reads `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which lags the `bd` SQLite DB.
- Closing the 40 beads was done by hand-running 40 `bd close` commands; one silently missed (write race) and one (downstream-app-9wup) was correctly blocked by an open child (downstream-app-7ftc) — all handled manually, off-tool.

## Children
1. (P1) Exclude bd-management commits from shipped detection.
2. (P1) Read authoritative bead status, not stale issues.jsonl.
3. (P2) apply/--close mode: deterministic batch close.
close_reason: epic complete

title: stale-beads: exclude bd-management commits (chore(bd|beads): file/update, spec()) from shipped detection
description:
## Problem

`bk guard stale-beads` flags any open/in_progress bead whose id appears in a shipped commit subject. But some subjects NAME a bead without shipping it — they file or spec it. On the downstream-app run, 7 of 48 findings (15%) were false positives:

- `spec(downstream-app-1k8x): ...` (#830) — spec commit (epic, children still open)
- `chore(bd): file downstream-app-5ctm ...` / `... km84 ...` (#1052)
- `chore(bd): file demo-app onboarding bead (downstream-app-h2ud) ...` (#1003)
- `chore(bd): file downstream-app-znpx ...` (#1009)
- `chore(beads): file downstream-app-cazl ...` (#1166)
- `chore(bd): update downstream-app-ix5u ...` (#1013)

## Deliverable

In the commit-subject classifier, treat bead-management commits as NON-shipping:
- Conventional-commit type `spec` → never shipping.
- Scope `chore(bd):` / `chore(beads):` (file / update / etc.) → never shipping.
- Only implementation types count as shipped: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor` (make this allowlist configurable via flag / config).

## Acceptance criteria

- Re-running on the downstream-app-shaped fixture flags ZERO of {1k8x, 5ctm, km84, h2ud, znpx, cazl, ix5u}.
- Still flags every genuine `feat(...)`/`fix(...)` shipped bead from the existing bkg-bqa.3 fixture.
- The implementation-type allowlist and the bd-management exclusions are covered by table-driven tests.
acceptance_criteria: Re-run on downstream-app fixture flags 0 of {1k8x,5ctm,km84,h2ud,znpx,cazl,ix5u}; still flags all genuine feat/fix; implementation-type allowlist + bd-management exclusions table-tested.
close_reason: shipped in #20

title: stale-beads: read authoritative bead status (bd DB), not lagging issues.jsonl
description:
## Problem

`bk guard stale-beads` reads bead status from `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which LAGS the authoritative `bd` SQLite DB. Observed on 2026-06-01:

- `bd close downstream-app-l6q` → `bd` reported "✓ Closed"; `bd list --json` showed status=closed.
- BUT `.beads/issues.jsonl` on disk still had `"id":"downstream-app-l6q" ... "status":"open"`.
- So `bk guard stale-beads` re-reported l6q as shipped-not-closed — a false positive caused purely by read-lag.

The daemon flushes the JSONL asynchronously, so any guard/board command run shortly after a mutation sees stale status.

## Deliverable

Source bead status from an authoritative, fresh read. Options (pick one, document the choice):
- Query `bd` directly (e.g. `bd list --json`) for status instead of parsing issues.jsonl, OR
- Detect the bd DB and read it, OR
- Add a `--refresh` that triggers/awaits a JSONL flush before reading, and document the lag otherwise.

Likely applies to `bk board` too (same JSONL source).

## Acceptance criteria

- Immediately after `bd close <id>`, `bk guard stale-beads` does NOT report `<id>` (no lag-induced false positive).
- Status reads are deterministic w.r.t. committed `bd` state.
- A regression test simulates DB-ahead-of-JSONL and asserts the guard uses the authoritative status.
acceptance_criteria: Immediately after bd close <id>, guard does not report <id>; status reads deterministic vs committed bd state; regression test simulates DB-ahead-of-JSONL.
close_reason: shipped in #21

title: stale-beads: --close/--apply mode (deterministic batch close, skip blocked, dry-run default)
description:
## Problem

`bk guard stale-beads` reports shipped-not-closed beads and emits a `bd_close_command` string per finding, but the agent still has to hand-run them. On 2026-06-01 that meant running 40 `bd close` commands in a shell loop — off-tool. Two things went wrong that a tool should own:
- One close silently missed on first pass (write race when hammering bd 40x); needed a manual retry.
- `downstream-app-9wup` could not close — `bd` refused: "blocked by open issues [downstream-app-7ftc] (use --force)". Handled manually.

## Deliverable

`bk guard stale-beads --close` (apply mode):
- DRY-RUN by default; require `--apply` to mutate.
- For each GENUINE shipped finding (after the Child .1 bd-management filter and Child .2 authoritative-status read), close it with reason `shipped in #<PR>`.
- Skip beads blocked by open issues (report them with the blocker id, e.g. 9wup←7ftc) unless `--force`.
- Race-safe / idempotent: verify status after each close; re-running is a clean no-op.
- Optional `--exclude <id,...>` to hold specific beads (e.g. a P0 pending verification like downstream-app-4i54).
- Print a summary: { closed, skipped_blocked, skipped_excluded, failed }.

## Acceptance criteria

- On the downstream-app-shaped fixture, `--apply` closes all genuine shipped beads in ONE command.
- Blocked beads are skipped with a clear blocker reason; `--force` overrides.
- Re-running `--apply` is a no-op (0 closed).
- Without `--apply`, nothing is mutated (dry-run shows the plan).
acceptance_criteria: --apply closes all genuine shipped beads in one command; skips blocked beads (e.g. 9wup<-7ftc) unless --force; re-run is no-op; without --apply nothing mutates.
close_reason: shipped in #22
